previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, diastolic dysfunction, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for chest pain radiating to the left arm, shortness of breath, and nausea. The pain was atypical and reproducible on chest wall palpation. Initial troponin was normal, second was mildly elevated at 0.04, but trended down to 0.01, in the setting of acute kidney injury likely due to reduced oral intake. EKG showed new right bundle branch block without ST changes. CT angiography ruled out pulmonary embolism. Stress test and echocardiogram showed no ischemia or wall motion abnormalities, with preserved ejection fraction of 57%. The chest pain responded to a GI cocktail and was attributed to gastroesophageal reflux. Her kidney function improved with hydration. Blood pressure was well-controlled inpatient, and labetalol was reduced to improve tolerance. She was discharged home on adjusted medications, including Maalox for symptom relief, with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider.

# ARF - Of note, Mrs ___ presented in acute renal failure 
during her most recent admit, with initial creatinine of 1.7, 
which improved to 1.3 with hydration. Her current ARF is 
attributable to pre-renal etiology, but can not exclude a 
component of ATN from hypotension and poor forward flow.  FeNa = 
0.5%, this is c/w pre-renal state.  Negative EOS, unlikely AIN.  
Her ARF resolved after IV hydration.
.
# Hypotension/hypertension - Thjs episode occurred in setting of 
taking lisinopril, amlodipine, clonidine, labetolol, and 
spironolactone all at once.  Her hypotension improved after 
holding her medication and IV hydration.  All of her blood 
pressure medications with exception of clonidine was restarted 
at the time of discharge.
.

the past two admissions. Unclear etiology, her TSH is mildly 
elevated; however, FT4 is within wnl. Iron studies are within 
normal limits, ferritin is elevated. Retic count is low, suggest 
an underproduction anemia, given normal WBC and Plt, ddx. 
includes infection, medications, renal disease, or acute blood 
loss.  She was told to follow up this issue as an outpatient.

# Nausea - This was likely due to medication - citalopram, 
though can not rule out infectious cause or gastroparesis.  Her 
citalopram was stopped.  Most LFT's are within normal limits.  
Alk Phos is presistently evelvated, unclear etiology given 
gallbladder was removed prior. C. diff, ova, parasites were

during this admission).  H. pylori, AMA, IgG, IgM, RUS were 
negative.  Still need to follow up on VIP at discharge.  Her 
symptoms were controlled if she avoided oral intake, not very 
well controlled on zofran and reglan.  Her symptoms improved but 
were not completely resolved at the time of her discharge.  She 
was told to follow up with her GI doctor as an outpatient for a 
gastric emptying study.
